chunks: Ali ibn Abdullah al-Warraq (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Mehrawayh al-Qazvini said: Dawood ibn Sulayman al-Ghazi narrated from Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him), from his father, from his forefathers, from the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) that he said:

The world is all ignorance except for the positions of knowledge. All knowledge is a proof except what is acted upon. All actions are out of hypocrisy except what is sincere. And sincerity is subject to danger until the servant looks at what he will end with.

key_terms.يُخْتَمُ لَهُ: He will end with (his final state/outcome)

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between knowledge, action, and sincerity in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: This profound chain of narration, transmitted through Imam al-Rida (s) to Imam Ali (s), establishes a rigorous spiritual diagnostic tool for self-purification (tazkiyah). It highlights the Shia emphasis on the inseparability of knowledge and action, warning that even sincere deeds remain vulnerable to hidden ostentation until the final outcome validates the heart's purity.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 28-25 Ali ibn Abdullah al-Warraq - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Mehrawayh al-Qazvini quoted on the authority of Dawood ibn Soleiman al-Qadhi, on the authority of Abil Hassan Ali ibn Musa Al-Ridha (s), on the authority of his father (s), on the authority of his forefathers (s), on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful (s), “

The world is all ignorance except for the positions of knowledge. All knowledge is considered to be a proof against man,unless it is acted accordingly. All acts are out of hypocrisy, unless they are done sincerely. Sincerity is subject to danger unless a servant (i.e. a person) ponders over what his final ending will be.”
